brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Five full-depth hex bins (hex-bin-full) on the level-0 full bases at (0,0), (1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (-1,-1) serve as book shelves, joined by 4 full bases plus north and south half bases. Mesh check is clear. Book props did not fit inside the bins, so no books are staged.
Two drawers: drawer:0#-1,1#cut on the south-half base at (-1,1) and drawer:0#0,-1#cut on the north-half base at (0,-1). Both were accepted by the configurator.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only and has no load rating. The printed PETG parts and M6 joints have not been load-tested, so I cannot verify or claim a 50 kg rating. The build is a lightly loaded design, not a certified one. Joints are locked with lockJoints (7 joint bolts); the BOM notes that M6 bolts should be hand-tightened to about 2 N.m.
capOpenFaces was refused with MESH_CLASH (hex-cap-edge-solid-m would run into hex-drawer-frame-s, 4.49 mm). The rollback kept the build clear, so 21 open faces remain uncapped.

finish.summary: I built a 6-base hex shelf unit with five full-depth bins for books and two drawers, with joints locked and a clear mesh check. The 50 kg load rating cannot be verified in the configurator and is unmet. The open-face cap house rule clashed with a drawer frame, so 21 faces are left open.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
